seo.title: Kimi CLI vs HagiCode: Features and Comparison
seo.description: Kimi CLI is now Kimi Code CLI, Moonshot AI's terminal coding agent; HagiCode is a workbench that runs it. Compare features, pricing and when each fits.

summary: Kimi CLI, now called Kimi Code CLI, is Moonshot AI's terminal coding agent; HagiCode is a workbench that can run it as an executor. This page compares features, access and cost, and when the CLI alone is enough.

content: Kimi CLI is Moonshot AI's terminal coding agent. The original Python project has been archived and replaced by Kimi Code CLI from the same team, which still installs a `kimi` command. HagiCode is a desktop and web workbench that launches `kimi` as one of its Agent CLIs and adds parallel sessions, proposals and commits around it. It does not replace Kimi and it does not sell Kimi access.

If you want a fast single-binary agent in your terminal, and perhaps in Zed or JetBrains over ACP, stay with Kimi alone. Add HagiCode when you run several tasks at once or want a spec-driven workflow on top of the same login.

sections.title: Kimi CLI vs HagiCode at a glance

cells: What it is
Moonshot AI's terminal coding agent; the original Kimi CLI is archived and succeeded by Kimi Code CLI (MIT)
Desktop and web AI programming workbench that drives Agent CLIs you install
Interface and platforms
Terminal UI with the `kimi` command; macOS, Linux, Windows (Git for Windows needed)
Desktop app for Windows, macOS, Linux; Docker Compose container; Microsoft Store edition
Pricing and licensing
Kimi Code is in Kimi memberships from Plus up (Go excludes it), or use a Moonshot Open Platform API key; see kimi.com pricing
Desktop and Container free; Store edition free with optional one-time TurboEngine purchase
Model and provider access
Kimi models out of the box; other compatible providers can be configured
Hosts no models; uses whatever `kimi` is signed in with, so cost stays with Moonshot
Parallel work
One session per terminal; built-in subagents (coder, explore, plan)
Several concurrent sessions across repos, managed from an Agents view
Spec and planning workflow
Plan subagent and plugins; no proposal lifecycle
OpenSpec proposals: propose, validate, apply, archive; 3 concurrent on free editions, 32 with TurboEngine
Git and commit handling
Runs shell and Git commands in the session; no dedicated commit workflow
AI-composed commits, Git management, GitHub integration, embedded Code Server editor
Setup effort
One install script (no Node.js needed), then `/login`
Install HagiCode Desktop, with a working, signed-in `kimi` already on the machine
Best for
Developers who want a fast terminal agent on Kimi models, or an ACP agent in their editor
Developers running several tasks or repos who want a GUI and a spec discipline

items.title: Kimi models out of the box, other providers optional
content: Run `/login`, choose Kimi Code OAuth or a Moonshot AI Open Platform API key, and you are on Kimi models. The CLI can also be configured for other compatible providers, so it is not welded to one backend.

items.title: Single binary, quick start
content: Kimi Code CLI ships as a single binary with fast startup and a purpose-built terminal UI, and the install script does not need Node.js. On Windows it needs Git for Windows, with `KIMI_SHELL_PATH` for a custom Git Bash location.

items.title: Subagents, hooks and plugins
content: It includes `coder`, `explore` and `plan` subagents, lifecycle hooks, a plugin ecosystem and conversational MCP setup with `/mcp-config`. It also accepts video input, which is uncommon among terminal agents.

items.title: Editor integration through ACP
content: Run `kimi acp` and Zed, JetBrains or another ACP client can drive it, so the same agent works in terminal and editor. Migration is gentle: on first launch it offers to import `~/.kimi/` config, MCP servers, history and sessions, or you can run `kimi migrate`.

sections.title: When to choose Kimi CLI, and when to choose HagiCode

items: You want a fast, single-binary terminal agent and are happy on Kimi models.
You already have a Kimi membership with Kimi Code (Plus or higher) or a Moonshot API key.
You use Zed or JetBrains and want the same agent over ACP in your editor.
You like subagents, hooks and plugins configured in the terminal.
You work on one task at a time and want no extra application.
You run several Kimi tasks across repositories and want the sessions side by side.
You want an OpenSpec proposal, validation and archive step before the agent edits code.
You prefer to review tool calls and diffs in a GUI, with AI-composed commits and Code Server.
You want Vault notes and Monospecs to carry context between Kimi sessions and repositories.
You mix Agent CLIs (Kimi, Claude Code, Codex and others) and want one workspace.

blocks.title: Where HagiCode is not the right tool
content: Headless CI and scripted one-shot runs: call `kimi` directly.
You only want a terminal, or a quick question in an editor you already use over ACP.
Teams that do not want proposal and spec discipline; free editions also cap concurrent proposals at 3.
It needs `kimi` installed and signed in first, so it adds setup compared with Kimi alone.
If you still run the archived Kimi CLI, move to Kimi Code CLI first: its repository says existing Kimi CLI installations will stop working.

sections.title: Using Kimi CLI together with HagiCode

content: HagiCode starts the `kimi` executable you already installed, in its ACP mode (`kimi acp`), and shows the session in its own interface. Your install, `/login` and Moonshot billing stay as they were.
Nothing is locked in: your repositories stay ordinary Git repositories and you can run `kimi` in a terminal at any time.

items: 1. Install Kimi Code CLI (`curl -fsSL https://code.kimi.com/kimi-code/install.sh | bash` on macOS or Linux, or `irm https://code.kimi.com/kimi-code/install.ps1 | iex` on Windows) and run `/login`.
2. Install HagiCode Desktop (free) for Windows, macOS or Linux.
3. In HagiCode, choose Kimi as the Agent CLI for a session.
4. Open a repository and start a session or an OpenSpec proposal.
5. Expect Kimi models and Moonshot billing as before; HagiCode adds workflow around them.
6. To go back to plain Kimi, open a terminal in the same repository and run `kimi`.

blocks.title: What works for Kimi CLI inside HagiCode
content: Works: parallel sessions, OpenSpec proposals, AI commits, Code Server, Vault, Monospecs and the unified tool-call view with Kimi.
Does not apply to Kimi: interactive questions (Claude, Pi, OMP and Reasonix only) and the agent work panel (Claude only).
HagiCode relies on the `kimi acp` interface, which Kimi Code CLI also documents; features that exist only in the Kimi terminal UI stay there.

sections.title: What HagiCode adds on top of any agent

items.title: Parallel sessions and Agents management
content: Kimi gives you one conversation per terminal. HagiCode can keep several Kimi sessions running across repositories and list them in one Agents view.

items.title: OpenSpec proposals
content: Kimi's plan subagent helps within a session. An OpenSpec proposal sits above it: written, validated, applied and archived, so the reason for a change outlives the chat.

items.title: AI commits and Code Server
content: HagiCode composes the commit message from what Kimi changed, and the embedded Code Server lets you check the edits without leaving the workbench.

items.title: Monospecs and Vault
content: Monospecs lets a Kimi session span several repositories; Vault holds notes that outlast any one session.

items.title: One tool-call view and optional TokenMonitor
content: Kimi's tool calls show in the same layout as other agents' calls, and an optional TokenMonitor can show usage in the status bar. Access and cost remain Moonshot's.

items: Kimi Code CLI is a fast, extensible terminal agent with ACP editor support; if one terminal and one task fits you, it is enough on its own.
HagiCode is a workbench layer that runs `kimi` underneath, adding sessions, proposals and commits rather than models.
Check that you are on Kimi Code CLI, not the archived Kimi CLI, before adding HagiCode.

faq.question: Is Kimi CLI free?
faq.answer: The CLI is open source, but model access is not free: Kimi Code is included in Kimi memberships from the Plus tier up (the Go tier excludes it), and you can alternatively use a Moonshot Open Platform API key. Plans and prices on kimi.com change, so check the pricing page.

faq.question: Is Kimi CLI still maintained?
faq.answer: The original Kimi CLI repository is archived and no longer maintained. It was replaced by Kimi Code CLI (MIT licence) from the same team, and the repository says existing Kimi CLI installations will stop working.

faq.question: How do I install Kimi CLI?
faq.answer: Install Kimi Code CLI with `curl -fsSL https://code.kimi.com/kimi-code/install.sh | bash` (macOS, Linux), `irm https://code.kimi.com/kimi-code/install.ps1 | iex` (Windows), `brew install kimi-code` or `npm install -g @moonshot-ai/kimi-code`. Then run `kimi` and `/login`.

faq.question: Can I use Kimi CLI with HagiCode?
faq.answer: Yes. Install Kimi and sign in, then choose Kimi as the Agent CLI in HagiCode, which launches `kimi acp`. Billing stays with Moonshot.

faq.question: Kimi CLI vs HagiCode: which should I pick?
faq.answer: Use Kimi alone for a fast terminal or editor agent. Add HagiCode for parallel sessions, OpenSpec proposals and a GUI over the same CLI.
